items.title: ‘हिंदू राष्ट्र’ से ‘आई लव मोदी’ कैंपेन तक: कौन है सीजेपी का कथित बागी मनीष ब्रह्मभट्ट
items.summary: कई दिनों तक न्यूज़ एजेंसी एएनआई और कई टेलीविजन चैनलों पर एक ही कहानी छाई रही कि कॉकरेच जनता पार्टी (सीजेपी) के भीतर विद्रोह हो गया है. इस कहानी का पूरा आधार एक अकेला व्यक्ति हैं, मनीष ब्रह्मभट्ट, जिन्होंने 3 सितंबर को सीजेपी से अलग होकर एक नया संगठन, सीजेपी (डेमोक्रेटिक) , बनाने का ऐलान किया. मीडिया ने इसे संगठन के भीतर वास्तविक संकट के तौर पर पेश किया, मगर ज्यादातर कवरेज में यह नहीं बताया गया कि आखिर मनीष ब्रह्मभट्ट हैं कौन. एक घोषणा जो सुर्खी बन गई 3 सितंबर को एएनआई ने ब्रह्मभट्ट के लॉन्च कार्यक्रम का 56 मिनट से लंबा वीडियो अपने यूट्यूब चैनल पर लाइव दिखाया. कुछ ही घंटों में इसके क्लिप डिजिटल और टेलीविजन मीडिया में हर तरफ फैल गए. एएनआई ने खुद 13 मिनट का एक क्लिप काटकर चलाया, जिसका शीर्षक था - 'सीजेपी रेबल मनीष ब्रह्मभट्ट अलेज आप ऑफ फंडिंग कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी एंड दीप्के, अनाउंसेज़ स्प्लिट’ इससे अलग एएनआई ने करीब सवा दो मिनट का वीडियो भी साझा किया. इसमें रिपोर्टर मनीष से बात कर रहे हैं. यहां ब्रह्मभट्ट ने आरोप लगाया कि सीजेपी की कोर कमेटी, आम आदमी पार्टी (आप) के इशारे पर चल रही है और केजरीवाल के कहने पर भाजपा से लड़ रही है. एएनआई ने इन दावों को बार-बार, हर बार सीजेपी में फूट के सबूत के तौर पर प्रसारित किया. दिलचस्प बात यह है कि इसी एजेंसी ने 20 जुलाई को सीजेपी के संसद मार्च के दौरान छात्रों की पिटाई से जुड़ा एक भी क्लिप या साउंडबाइट अपने एक्स अकाउंट पर नहीं दिखाया था. सीजेपी का पक्ष न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री से बातचीत में सीजेपी के सौरव दास ने कहा कि एक खास व्यक्ति को उभारकर संगठन में दरार दिखाने की यह कोशिश उसी अभियान की कड़ी है, जिसके तहत दिल्ली में सीजेपी के प्रदर्शन के दौरान मीडिया के एक वर्ग ने संगठन को बदनाम करने की कोशिश की थी. ब्रह्मभट्ट के संस्थापक सदस्य होने के दावे को दास ने पूरी तरह गलत बताया. उनके मुताबिक, ब्रह्मभट्ट न कभी संस्थापक सदस्य रहे, न कोर कमेटी का हिस्सा और न ही उन्होंने कभी किसी सीजेपी कार्यक्रम में मंच साझा किया. दास ने बताया कि अगस्त में जब ब्रह्मभट्ट छत्रपति संभाजीनगर में अभिजीत दीप्के के घर आए थे, तभी उनकी और अन्य सदस्यों की उनसे पहली मुलाकात हुई थी. उन्होंने कहा, 'आशुतोष (रांका) और मैंने उनकी बात सुनी लेकिन वहां भी उन्होंने हंगामा खड़ा कर दिया.' प्राइमटाइम पर बढ़ा-चढ़ाकर पेश की गई कहानी रिपब्लिक टीवी ने 3 सितंबर को इस मामले को पूरा प्राइमटाइम स्लॉट दिया. एडिटर-इन-चीफ अर्णब गोस्वामी ने ब्रह्मभट्ट को सीजेपी का ‘प्रमुख चेहरा और संस्थापक सदस्य’ बताया. अर्णब ने उन्हें 'अंदरूनी सूत्र' बताते कहा कि वह अब सीजेपी के ‘आप’ के साथ संबंधों को लेकर संगठन के खिलाफ खड़े हो गए हैं. चैनल ने बार-बार सीजेपी के संस्थापकों की तस्वीरें आप नेताओं के साथ दिखाईं. यहां मनीष के दावे को आगे बढ़ाते हुए अर्णब ने सीजेपी को आप की 'बी टीम' करार दिया. और इसी को लेकर कार्यक्रम म

items.title: Confused by the debate over India’s 7.8% GDP growth? Here’s a simple explanation
items.summary: Bade bade deshon mein aisi choti choti baatein hoti rehti hai – Javed Siddiqui, Dilwale Dulhaniya Le Jayenge (1995) India’s gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 7.8% has been in the news all through this month. Edit and oped pages of newspapers are buzzing. So are digital and social media. As is the University of WhatsApp. But the trouble is that none of this writing manages to explain the 7.8% growth in simple English. Why? Economists and analysts who can explain such things, aren’t really used to explaining things. As John Lanchester writes in How to Speak Money : “As your vocabulary becomes more specific, more useful, more effective, it also becomes more exclusive. You are talking to a smaller audience.” This is an attempt to explain India’s 7.8% GDP growth rate in simple English. India’s GDP during the period April to June 2026 grew 7.8% in comparison to April to June 2025. GDP is a measure of the economic size of a country during a particular period. And by that definition GDP growth is a measure of economic growth. The trouble is – and as I explain here – an economic growth of 7.8% doesn’t pass the basic smell test of the lived experiences of people’s daily lives. So, how is the economy growing at a rate of 7.8%? The answer is slightly long, and perhaps even complicated in parts. Let’s dig in. No explanations on previous GDP figures The 7.8% economic growth rate is the real GDP growth rate. It adjusts for rise in prices or inflation. India’s nominal GDP growth rate during April to June 2026 was 10.3%. The nominal GDP growth rate does not adjust for rise in prices. How did we arrive at the 10.3% growth rate? The nominal GDP during April to June 2026 was Rs 88.26 lakh crore. During April to June 2025 it was Rs 80 lakh crore, meaning that the Indian economy grew 10.3% in nominal terms. From this we subtract the price rise or inflation and get a real GDP growth rate of 7.8%. QED. Well, hold on, hold on… Now, in February 2026, India moved to a new method of calculating the GDP. This method has a base year of 2022-23. The earlier method had a base year of 2011-12. Changing the base year is something that happens now and then because the structure of the economy changes. Like in 2011-12, India’s economy had nowhere as many smartphones as it does now. Or the fact that there was no Netflix, JioHotstar or Amazon Prime for that matter. Their source was one man, Manish Brahmbhatt, who, on September 3, announced he was breaking away to form a rival outfit called CJP(Democratic) or CJP(D). They treated it as a genuine internal crisis, but what most of them left out was who Manish Brahmbhatt actually is. The announcement that became a headline ANI uploaded Brahmbhatt’s launch event running for over 56 minutes to its YouTube channel on September 3. Within hours, clips of it were circulating across digital and television media. ANI itself cut a 13-minute clip titled, “CJP rebel Manish Brahmbhatt alleges AAP of funding Cockroach Janata Party & Dipke, announces split.” A separate 2-minute-21-second soundbite captured Brahmbhatt’s central charge that the CJP’s core committee was taking directions from the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and fighting the BJP “at Kejriwal’s behest” to help parties opposed to it. ANI aired his claims repeatedly, each time framing them as proof of a split inside CJP – a notable development given that the same outlet did not broadcast a single clip on X of students being beaten, or their soundbites, during CJP’s march to Parliament on July 20. Responding to the claim that Brahmbhatt was a founding member of CJP, Das said this was “completely incorrect”. He stated that Brahmbhatt had never been a founding member or part of the core committee and had never appeared on stage at a CJP event. items.summary: “I cracked the skull of Nishu’s father. Do you know which section this crime attracts? Section 307. He needed 60 stitches. The man who was about to die was being taken away in an ambulance. His daughter was standing outside the police station and saying that if her father did not get justice, she would consume poison and die. But I was not even jailed. The world should know this. I was roaming around freely the entire night.” When Hindutva fanatic Swatantra Bhardwaj said this on a podcast, he was not merely recounting an alleged assault, he was boasting about it, while pointing to his purported proximity to power. In the same podcast, Bhardwaj claimed BJP cabinet ministers Kapil Mishra and Chirag Paswan, as well as Prime Minister Narendra Modi, were his “bade bhaiyas” (big brothers), and hence there was no action against him. Hindutva extremist Swatantra Bhardwaj spoke about attacking the father of a CJP protester during a podcast. (@Sarcaztick) September 2, 2026 When the video began circulating widely on social media around September 2, it triggered demands for his arrest. It was only after CJP representatives protested outside the Parliament Street station and online outrage mounted, that the Delhi police added more stringent Sections to the FIR. items.title: Gaurav Bhatia files ₹2 crore defamation case in Delhi HC against CJP's Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka
items.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader and Senior Advocate Gaurav Bhatia has filed a defamation case before the Delhi High Court against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and its leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Bhatia has sought ₹2 crore in damages and an injunction against the CJP leaders. He sued the CJP and its leaders after an AI-generated graphic falsely attributed remarks about Swatantra Bhardwaj to Bhatia. Bhardwaj is accused of assault on the father of CJP activist Nishu Azad. The post stated that Bhatia called Bhardwaj a "dimagi naxal". Das shared the graphic on X, prompting Bhatia to deny making the remarks and give him 24 hours to delete the post and issue an unconditional apology. Das, who later deleted the post, clarified on his X account that it was AI-generated, but asked Bhatia whether he “disagreed” with the AI-generated statement. CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka allegedly amplified the disputed post by reposting the graphic from Das's account, adding a caption mocking BJP leaders. Ranka had earlier joined Das and other CJP members in demanding action against Bharadwaj over an alleged assault on the father of CJP activist Nishu Azad.

items.title: Supreme Court asks Centre to consider setting up expert panel for legal education reforms
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday asked the Central government to consider setting up an expert body to examine issues concerning legal education in India [Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay v Union of India & Ors] . A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana held that such a body was particularly relevant in the present era. “This is an important matter. The Union of India should consider it. This is an era of expert bodies. There should be an expert body on legal education,” said CJI Kant. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The Court made the observation while hearing a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) filed by Advocate Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay. The plea sought the constitution of a Legal Education Commission or expert committee comprising educationists, jurists, retired judges, advocates and professors. It also sought a review of the existing legal education framework, including the syllabus, curriculum and duration of Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.) and Master of Laws (LL.M.) courses. The petition particularly challenged the rationale for the existing 5-year integrated BA.LL.B. and BBA.LL.B. courses. It argues that the duration is disproportionate to the law-related curriculum and places an excessive financial and time burden on students. "New Education Policy 2020 promotes 04 years Graduation Courses in all Professional and Academic Courses but BCI has not taken appropriate steps to review the existing Syllabus, Curriculum and the Duration of the LLB and LLM Courses," submitted the petition. According to the plea, the 5-year integrated courses require students to study subjects such as History, Sociology, Economics and Political Science alongside core law subjects. It argues that a 4-year standalone law degree would be sufficient and would be more consistent with the objectives of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. "The purpose of any course is to provide just and essential knowledge required for career and not to barrage a student with all kinds of knowledge as they are innumerable. In no way is BA essential to study B.Law. It is good if Student know it, but it is entirely superfluous," argued the plea. It cited the UGC’s decision allowing students with 4-year undergraduate degrees to directly appear for NET and pursue PhD programmes. items.title: After Kerala High Court nudge, State renames mental health institutions as Happiness and Wellness Centres
items.summary: The Kerala government told the High Court on Tuesday that the State has issued a notification renaming State-run mental health centres as ' Happiness and Wellness Centres. ' [The High Court Legal Aid Committee v The State of Kerala] A bench of Justices Devan Ramachandran and Basant Balaji was informed by Advocate General Jaju Babu that a notification to that effect was issued on September 7. " The learned Advocate General Jaju Babu informs us that the notification renaming the Centres as ‘Happiness and Wellness Centres’ has already been issued and handed over. We see that the notification mentioned by the learned Advocate General has placed on record the notification no [so and so], dated 07.09.2026, and the same has been placed on record along with the memo dated 08.09.2026, " the Court recorded. The development came about after the Court had earlier raised concerns over the stigma associated with mental health institutions. The proceedings arose from a petition initiated by the High Court Legal Aid Committee concerning conditions at such centres in the State. Justice Devan Ramachandran and Justice Basant Balaji During the hearing, the Senior Counsel appearing for the Indian Medical Association (IMA) and Indian Psychiatric Society (IPS) said that the organisations wanted to raise certain objections to the new name before the government. The Court permitted the IMA and IPS to submit their suggestions to the Principal Secretary of the Health Department on or before September 14. " The said authority or such other competent authority as may be found fit by the government will hear the representatives of both these entities or any other doctor who may be interested, at 11 AM on 16.09.2026. For report of deliberations 22.09.2026. " The Court has also granted one more week's time to the Advocate General to get instructions on whether the government is addressing the issues relating to shortage of staff, security of the perimeter, uninterrupted, availability of medicines and provision of vehicles, at the centres. Senior Counsel VV Ashokan instructed by advocate Litto Palathinkal appeared for the IMA and IPS. Advocate V Ramkumar Nambiar served as the amicus curiae.

items.title: Calcutta High Court transfers hate speech case against Mahua Moitra to MP/MLA Court
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on September 7 transferred the hate speech case against Trinamool Congress Member of Parliament Mahua Moitra from a Magistrate court to a special MP/MLA court [Mahua Moitra vs. The State of West Bengal & Ors.]. A Division Bench comprising Justice Debangsu Basak and Justice Aryak Dutt said that a regular magistrate court lacks the jurisdiction to entertain cases against lawmakers. "In the facts and circumstances of the present case, there is a complaint case as against the petitioner before us who is a Member of Parliament. Complaint registered as against the Member of Parliament was sought to be taken cognizance of by the learned 3rd Judicial Magistrate, Krishnagar, Nadia. Such Court is not the designated Court for the purpose of trying an offence against a Member of Parliament and Member of State Legislature," the Court held. Hence, it directed that the proceedings be transferred from the court of the Magistrate court at Krishnanagar in Nadia to the designated special court for MP/MLA cases situated at Bidhannagar in North 24 Parganas. The special MP/MLA court at Bidhannagar must take up the matter afresh at the pre-cognizance stage, the Court added. The complaint case against Moitra accused her of making objectionable remarks, including those insulting women. The Krishnanagar Magistrate court had issued an arrest warrant against Moitra on August 19 after she failed to appear before it. Moitra then approached the High Court invoking challenging the cognizance taken by the Magistrate. The High Court on August 19 stayed the arrest warrant . In its final order passed on September 7, the High Court focused on the jurisdictional competence of the Magistrate to hear the case. The Bench observed that as per Supreme Court directions in the case of Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay v. Union of India , proceedings against Members of Parliament or State legislatures must be dealt with expeditiously by designated special courts. Hence, it directed the District Judge at Nadia to immediately transmit all case records to the District Judge at North 24 Parganas, who will subsequently forward them to the special MP/MLA court at Bidhannagar. "On receipt of such records, learned Judicial Magistrate, Special Court is requested to proceed in accordance with law as against the petitioner and the other accused treating the proceedings as one of a pre-cognizance stage," the High Court said. items.title: Will summon your officers if you don't decide on remission plea by Dara Singh: Supreme Court to Odisha
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday warned that it would summon officials of the Odisha government if the State's Sentence Review Board continues to delay its decision on a remission plea filed by Dara Singh, who is serving a life sentence for the 1999 murder of Australian missionary Graham Staines and his two minor sons [ Rabindra Kumar Pal @ Dara Singh v. State of Odisha ]. A Bench of Justices Manoj Misra and Vijay Bishnoi was hearing Singh’s petition seeking premature release from prison. “ Take a decision; otherwise, we will summon your officers, ” the Court said. This was after Odisha government's counsel sought an adjournment of the matter today, stating that Advocate-on-Record (AoR) was suffering from a viral infection. The Court pointed out that the case was adjourned several times earlier for the State's Sentence Review Board to make a decision, to no avail. “ You (State authority) cannot avoid taking a decision. You have to decide one way or the other. For two years, you have been delaying the decision. Accept or reject the plea, but take a decision. Inform the Court, ” Justice Manoj Misra said. Justices Manoj Misra and Vijay Bishnoi Dara Singh was part of a mob that killed Graham Staines and his two minor sons in 1999. The mob had set alight a vehicle in which the Staines were taking shelter for the night. The Supreme Court judgment convicting Singh recorded that the intention of the mob "was to teach a lesson to Graham Staines about his religious activities, namely, converting poor tribals to Christianity." Singh was initially sentenced to death by the trial court. The Orissa High Court subsequently commuted the sentence to life imprisonment, which was upheld by the Supreme Court in 2011. Singh later sought a remission (premature release from prison). In a remission petition filed before the top court, Singh stated that he is over 60 years old and has spent more than 24 years in prison. He claimed that he regrets his actions and is now reformed. The plea also stated that the offences were committed in his youth amid an impassioned desire to “safeguard and defend Mother India.” Singh also claimed that he had never been released on parole. On August 19, the top court had pulled up Odisha's Sentence Review Board after being informed that it had yet to decide on Singh’s remission plea. items.title: Supreme Court extends tenure of 3 NGT members; AG says 229 tribunal members' tenure extended
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday allowed two Judicial Members and one Expert Member of the National Green Tribunal (NGT) whose once-extended terms expire today to continue in office despite their crossing the retirement age, until fresh member appointments are made. The direction was passed by a Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana to ensure that the NGT's functioning is not hampered until new appointments are made to fill vacancies at the tribunal. "In order to ensure that the day-to-day functioning of the National Green Tribunal is not hampered, we direct continuation of the two Judicial Members and one Expert Member as an interim measure till fresh appointments are made in their place," the Court ordered. The order was passed after Attorney General (AG) R Venkataramani apprised the Court of the position concerning vacancies in various tribunals during the transition to a new regime under the Tribunal Reforms Act, 2026 . Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The Court had earlier extended the tenure of chairpersons and members of various tribunals whose terms were due to expire between March and September until September 8, subject to the applicable maximum age limits. The NGT Bar Association later expressed concerns that three zonal Benches of the NGT could become non-functional from September 8 onwards with the expiry of some of the tribunal members' extended tenures. The association had pointed out that the NGT Act does not permit a single-member Bench. As such, the expiry of the members' extended terms on September 8 could cripple the Southern and Western Zone Benches of the NGT, the association had submitted. Today, AG Venkataramani informed the Court that under Section 24 of the 2026 Tribunals Act, 248 members serving on different tribunals were eligible to have their terms extended because they had not yet completed the five-year term prescribed under the new law. He further submitted that extension orders have already been issued for 229 members, while orders for the remaining 19 were being issued on Tuesday. items.title: Party with sufficient interest can participate in CCI proceedings to aid public interest: Delhi High Court
items.summary: A person, association or enterprise having sufficient interest in a competition law case can be allowed to participate in the proceedings before the Competition Commission of India (CCI) if such participation would aid the CCI and further public interest, the Delhi High Court has held [Ultratech Cement Vs CCI]. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia made the observation while dismissing an appeal by UltraTech Cement against the CCI’s decision to make the Builders’ Association of India (BAI) a party to the proceedings concerning alleged cartelisation by cement manufacturers. The Court said the case initiated by the CCI was primarily intended to achieve public interest by checking anti-competitive practices and protecting consumers. It added that impleadment does not determine the rights of either the party under investigation or the party being impleaded. Its purpose is to assist the CCI in reaching a proper conclusion on alleged violations of competition law. items.title: We need to have more brown in international arbitration: Karnataka HC CJ Vibhu Bakhru at India ADR Week
items.summary: Karnataka High Court Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru on Monday called for more diversity of arbitrators in international arbitration. During a fireside chat with Senior Advocate Aditya Sondhi at the Bengaluru leg of the India ADR Week 2026, hosted by Mumbai Centre for International Arbitration (MCIA), Justice Bakhru was asked whether India needed separate legislation to govern international arbitration. The judge said, “Well, personally I don't think we require multiple Acts…if you have very frequent amendments, if you have very frequent changes in the statutory structure, possibly the results may be amplified.” Responding to a question on the differences between international arbitration and arbitration in the Global South, he said, “What is the aspiration of the country as far as arbitration is concerned? Well, one of the standing issues is about diversity. You need to have more brown in international arbitration than there is in the Global South. It's possible that that doesn't require an enactment.” MCIA - Bangalore Justice Bakhru also called for more scrutiny and quality control in arbitration. He said, “I've always been a firm advocate that we do require QCs in arbitration laws. I think more than 50% of the issues that arise in Section 34 would challenge the arbitration law, would not arise if it had a four-eye check, just as all firms do that, before you turn on the document and give it to anybody else.” In her speech, Karnataka High Court Justice Tara Vitasta Ganju spoke on the next phase of reform of the Arbitration Act. She said that it should focus less on adding isolated provisions and more on designing arbitration as a coherent statutory system. “The statute must address the precise points at which arbitration loses time and legitimacy. Jurisdiction appointments, internal protection, procedural objections, extensions of pleas and so on.” On judicial interference in arbitral awards and delays in the process, she said, “The discipline at the appellate stage is of larger concern. items.title: Is Andar Bahar a game of skill or chance? Karnataka HC refers issue to larger bench
items.summary: A single judge Bench of the Karnataka High Court on Tuesday held that the question of whether Andar Bahar is a game of skill or a game of chance requires reconsideration by a larger Bench. Andar Bahar is a card game in which players place bets on whether a card matching a designated card will appear first on a box referred to as "Andar" or on the "Bahar" box. Justice Suraj Govindaraj today expressed doubts over the correctness of a 1977 High Court ruling, E Eranna v. State of Karnataka , in which 14 persons said to have played Andar Bahar were acquitted of allegations that they had played outlawed games of chance (wagering or betting games). In E Eranna , a single-judge Bench of the High Court had reasoned that the prosecution did not show how Andar Bahar was a game of chance. " It was not categorically proved that ‘Andar Bahar’ is a game of chance and that these accused were playing that game," the High Court had ruled in the E Eranna judgment. This ruling has subsequently been cited time and again by other Benches of the Court to rule that Andar Bandar is a game of skill rather than an outlawed game of chance. Today, Justice Govindraj expressed reservations about this view. The Court observed that once the cards are shuffled and the deck is prepared for a game of Andar Bahar, the subsequent flow of cards is not dependent on the players' skill. “ There is absolutely no skill which would be involved in determining which card would flow from the deck when the game starts ... The number (of cards) being determined on the basis of the players or preset card, that the card [is] higher or below that particular number, would not require any skill ," the Court observed. Justice Suraj Govindraj Justice Govindraj, therefore, opined that Andar Bahar is a game of chance. However, since this view conflicted with the E Eranna ruling, the matter has now been referred to a larger Bench of the Court. “ The (question of the) game of Andhar Bahar not (being) a game of skill but game of chance would require re-consideration by larger bench to be constituted by Chief Justice, ” Justice Govindraj said. The Registry was accordingly directed to place the matter before the Chief Justice for the constitution of an appropriate Bench to reconsider the issue. The Court made the reference while considering a petition challenging criminal proceedings initiated under Sections 79 and 80 of the Karnataka Police Act against several persons found playing the card game in 2020. items.title: Nobody questions economic damage caused by Supreme Court judgments: Sajan Poovayya
items.summary: Senior Advocate Sajan Poovayya on Monday questioned why the economic consequences of Supreme Court judgments receive so little scrutiny, even in major commercial disputes involving governments and large corporations. Poovayya was speaking in Delhi at the launch of In-House Matters , a handbook on the modern general counsel authored by Pramod Rao , Ritvik Lukose and Balanand Menon . The book draws on the experiences of 30 leading general counsel across India. The senior advocate said, “ Nobody really questions the Supreme Court today on what's the economic damage that a judgment does or what's the economic cost." He added that judgments continued to be viewed largely through the lens of the “march of law”, rather than by asking what economic consequences they may produce. Poovayya said that this way of thinking had already changed in other parts of corporate law. Directors today, for instance, were expected to consider not merely their legal obligations to a company, but also how their decisions affected communities and the environment. In-house Matters He said that the role of a general counsel (GC) had also fundamentally changed over the past few decades. “ The simple question that we would ask 35 years ago to a general counsel was possibly, ‘Is it permissible in law?’ The question now has really turned to simply, ‘Should we do it ?’” According to Poovayya, GCs were increasingly becoming “keepers of institutional morality”. Their task was no longer confined to deciding whether something was legally permissible. They also had to consider what a decision would mean for the organisation years later. He described the modern GC as a lawyer, a “chief ethics officer” and a person expected to provide larger institutional direction. Former Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Chairman UK Sinha similarly said that GCs should become part of business strategy. Sinha said that the legal team had played a leading role when ICICI was converted from a development financial institution into a universal bank. He also referred to UTI's restructuring after the 2001 crisis and said that the idea behind the eventual structure had come from a lawyer within the institution. He added that legal teams could shape the “tone at the top” and help build institutional culture by ensuring rules were applied uniformly irrespective of seniority. Justice Amit Bansal directed MCD not to take any precipitative or coercive sealing action against Mahabelly's premises in Saidulajab. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday held that a company can face criminal prosecution even if the investigating agency has not identified or arraigned the particular employee or official through whom the concerned company acted [Sanofi India Ltd. Vs CBI]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and Manoj Misra made the ruling while dismissing an appeal by Sanofi India Ltd against the Karnataka High Court’s refusal to quash criminal proceedings arising from a CBI case. The Court said that at the stage of considering a petition to quash criminal proceedings under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the prosecution is not required in every case to identify the specific natural person through whom the company allegedly acted. “ What the chargesheet must disclose, on its face, is that the corporation itself has committed the offence, not that it has also identified the particular individual through whom it did so ,” the Court said. It added that a company’s role could be disclosed through allegations concerning its own conduct, decisions and dealings, even without naming the individual who carried them out. No Sanofi employee or official, however, was arraigned as an accused in the chargesheet. Sanofi argued that a company could not be prosecuted for an offence involving mens rea , or guilty intent, unless the prosecution identified the individual who represented the company’s “directing mind” or alter ego. items.title: ANI files appeal before Delhi HC challenging denial of interim relief in case against OpenAI
items.summary: News agency Asian News International (ANI) has filed an appeal before the Delhi High Court against a single-judge's order denying it interim relief in its copyright infringement suit against OpenAI, the owner of ChatGPT. The appeal against the July 24 order is listed for hearing on September 8 before a Division Bench of Justices V Kameswaro Rao and Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora . ANI is the first Indian media house to sue OpenAI for copyright violation . Justice V Kameswar Rao and Justice Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora In its interim injunction application before the single-judge, the agency had sought directions to OpenAI to stop storing, publishing, reproducing or using ANI's copyrighted works. Several other publications had also joined ANI in its case, including the Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA). The DNPA members include The Times Group, Hindustan Times, India Today Group, The Hindu and almost every major media house. However, the single-judge refused to pass such an order, holding that it would be against public interest. In his ruling, single-judge Justice Amit Bansal held that OpenAI's storage of news material published by ANI to train ChatGPT does not amount to copyright infringement. Notably, the single-judge said that irreparable injury would be caused not only to OpenAI but to public interest also if any interim injunction is granted in favour of ANI at this stage. The judge reasoned that ChatGPT has transformed information and is being used all around the world for beneficial purposes. ANI has now approached the division bench against the same. It is ANI's case that merely because its news content is publicly available, OpenAI does not get a right to exploit it or create copies of it to store. The news agency has said that in denying interim relief, the single-judge erred in the interpretation of the copyright law. items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has dismissed an anticipatory bail plea filed by suspended Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) Chairman Sahukar S Shivashankarappa in connection with the alleged veterinarians' recruitment scam [ Sahukar S Shivashankarappa v. State of Karnataka ]. Shivashankarappa is among the KPSC officials accused of having manipulated the recruitment process to favour certain candidates, including relatives of KPSC officials. A trial court rejected his anticipatory bail plea on August 11, prompting him to approach the High Court for relief. Justice S Vishwajith Shetty today noted that the allegations raised serious concerns. He observed that because of such irregularities in public exams and recruitment, people were losing faith in such processes. "Public is losing faith in the system of examination. We have seen so many meritorious students commit suicide in that NEET (because of NEET paper leaks). So many. What mistake have they made? What have they done? What is the loss that the family has suffered? It's not the question of just the result. There are so many issues that people are not able to come forward and answer. These things should be put to an end. Then and there, they (accused) should be arrested," the judge remarked. Justice S Vishwajith Shetty The case concerns alleged irregularities in the KPSC recruitment examination for 400 Veterinary Officer posts. The complaint alleged that relatives of KPSC officials secured unusually high marks, that some candidates were allegedly given access to the question paper before the examination, and that OMR sheets were tampered with. Middlemen allegedly approached candidates and promised to secure appointments for ₹70-80 lakhs, allegedly by manipulating their OMR marks. items.title: Supreme Court directs Centre, States to set up 449 exclusive NDPS courts within 6 months
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday directed the Central government, States, and Union Territories to take immediate steps to establish 449 exclusive courts for trial of cases under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act (NDPS Act). A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana issued the directive after taking on record a status report filed by the Union of India, which revealed that only 176 of the required 449 exclusive NDPS courts are presently operational across the country. The Court expressed concern over the alarming surge in narcotics cases nationwide and directed setting up 449 courts, preferably within six months. “Having regard to the current pendency of cases under the NDPS Act and the alarming increase in offences under the Act across the country, it is expedient and in the interest of justice that the requisite 449 exclusive NDPS courts be established at the earliest,” the Court recorded. The bench directed all States and Union Territories to urgently arrange the necessary court infrastructure and appoint judicial and administrative staff to bridge the deficit. The Court had previously instructed authorities to assess requirements to conduct these trials on a day-to-day basis and conclude them within one year. She added that operational courts have increased from 113 to 176. items.title: Marital Rape case: Supreme Court to decide hearing date on September 9
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to immediately defer the hearing in the batch of petitions challenging the marital rape exception. The Court rejected the request to postpone the hearing till November. A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana stated that it will hear the Union government on Wednesday, September 9, before fixing a date for final arguments. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The batch of matters before the top court stems primarily from a May 2022 split verdict of the Delhi High Court. While Justice Rajiv Shakdher had held Exception 2 to Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code (which immunises non-consensual sexual acts by a husband against his adult wife) to be unconstitutional, Justice C Hari Shankar upheld the exception, ruling that the legislature’s classification was based on intelligible differentia. Other petitions tagged with the batch include an appeal against a Karnataka High Court ruling that refused to quash marital rape charges framed against a husband under Section 376 IPC. The issue was mentioned by Senior Advocate Indira Jaising , who pointed out that the batch comprises eight matters listed as Item 108 on September 9. "The matter is listed on September 9 as Item 108 for final hearing. It is a group of eight matters, some of which challenge the constitutional validity of the marital rape exception. Four matters arise from a reference made following the split verdict of the Delhi High Court, while three are fresh petitions, including one filed in 2026. The Union has not filed a substantive affidavit in response, apart from raising a preliminary objection through a common order," she said. Jaising further submitted that copies of all petitions had not been exchanged among counsel, making it difficult to ascertain common legal grounds. She requested the Bench to fix a date for final hearing in November instead. Responding to the submission regarding the lack of a counter-affidavit from the Centre, CJI Kant remarked: "When it is a constitutional validity matter… what is the need for the counter?" Senior Advocate Karuna Nundy intervened to submit that the Union’s affidavit would be essential assistance to the Court. "It will be of some assistance, especially on such a question," Nundy said. Senior Advocate Siddhartha Dave informed the Bench that the matter involves distinct factual and legal matrices that have been clubbed together.

items.title: Senior Advocate DLN Rao passes away
items.summary: Senior Advocate DLN Rao , a veteran member of the Karnataka Bar and one of the country’s leading lawyers in mining law, passed away on Monday. Rao was a designated Senior Advocate of the Karnataka High Court and with more that five decades of experience at the bar. He had an extensive practice before the Karnataka High Court as well as the Supreme Court, particularly in matters concerning mining, land acquisition, infrastructure and public law. Rao is one of the foremost authorities in mining law. Rao also played a notable role in litigation surrounding Bengaluru's Namma Metro project. In 2010, the Karnataka High Court appointed him as amicus curiae in proceedings concerning the proposed underground Metro stretch between the Vidhana Soudha and the High Court through the Cubbon Park area. The Bench had sought his assistance considering the wider implications of the project. The High Court subsequently permitted the underground Metro project while imposing safeguards concerning restoration of land and protection of the green cover. Rao, while assisting the Court, had also raised issues concerning the trees that would be affected and the use of ancillary buildings connected with the project. The earlier deadline to submit the Aravalli panel's report expired on August 31. The expert panel, set up on the Court's orders earlier this year , had sought six months more - until February 28, 2027 - to submit its report on the definition and protection of the Aravalli Hills. However, the Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana took exception to the request, and said it was an attempt to keep the issue in cold storage till CJI Kant demits office. "The committee has basically asked for an adjournment till my retirement," remarked CJI Kant during the hearing today. CJI Kant will retire from office on February 9, 2027. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana The Court today directed the HPC to “work day and night”, if needed, and submit its report by November 30. No further extension will be granted, the Court said. While the Court accepted recommendations prohibiting mining in core or inviolate areas, it declined to impose a complete mining ban, observing that such prohibition could lead to illegal mining and criminalisation. items.title: Delhi HC summons Sudhir Chaudhary, DD News in defamation suit for branding activist as "anti-national"

Sherawat has sued Chaudhary and DD News over a show aired on the public broadcaster on August 27, when Chaudhary alleged that during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest, Sherawat was talking about destroying Parliament and creating a Nepal-like situation in India. The suit seeks ₹5 crore in damages. Justice Subramonium Prasad heard the case today and issued summons in the suit. The Court also issued notice on the interim injunction application filed by Sherawat, in which he has asked for directions to stop Chaudhary and other defendants from publishing/re-publishing or broadcasting the allegations. Justice Prasad said that the plea for interim injunction will be considered on September 22. "It is expected that on the next date of hearing, Defendants 1, 2 and 3 [Chaudhary, Essar and DD] would be ready for advancing arguments on the interim stay," the Court said in its order. items.title: We will not be browbeaten: Punjab and Haryana High Court in Punjab DA case
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Monday observed that the Court will not be browbeaten by any kind of tactics and will defend the oath of the Constitution. The comment by Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra was made during the hearing of applications related to pending Dearness Allowance (DA) of Punjab government employees and pensioners. Justice Mishra, who today took oath as the Chief Justice amid a brewing controversy over the Punjab government's opposition to his elevation, was sitting on a division bench along with Justice Rohit Kapoor when he made the observation. "This Court would be governed by the rule of law and this institution will not be browbeaten by any kind of tactics. So therefore, we will go strictly as per the law. The Court said it will neither be influenced by the submissions of the petitioners nor the government. "Either side, don't comment! You may have a lot of things to say or do, we will go by law. items.title: Supreme Court refuses to revive ₹363 crore GST demand against Vodafone Idea
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to revive a ₹363 crore Goods and Services Tax (GST) demand against Vodafone Idea after the Bombay High Court had quashed proceedings initiated against an entity that had ceased to exist following a merger. [Union of India v. Vodafone] A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and N Vinod Chandran dismissed the Centre’s appeal against the High Court ruling. During the brief hearing, the Bench questioned how proceedings could have been initiated against a non-existent entity after amalgamation. The dispute arose from a GST demand linked to the transfer of Vodafone Mobile Services Limited’s telecom tower business to ATC Telecom Infrastructure in 2017. Vodafone Mobile Services had entered into an agreement with ATC Telecom Infrastructure for sale of its tower business as a going concern on a slump-sale basis. Vodafone Mobile Services later merged with Vodafone India Limited and Idea Cellular Limited pursuant to an August 2018 order of the National Company Law Tribunal. The merger was also intimated to the GST authorities. In August 2024, the Directorate General of GST Intelligence issued a show-cause notice to Vodafone Mobile Services demanding ₹363 crore under the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, along with penalty. The department’s case was that the transfer of a going concern was an exempt supply and that the company was consequently not entitled to avail input tax credit to the extent claimed. An adjudication order was later passed in January 2025. Vodafone Idea challenged the proceedings before the Bombay High Court, arguing that Vodafone Mobile Services had ceased to exist following the merger and that proceedings could not be initiated against a non-existent entity. In April 2026, a Bench of Justices GS Kulkarni and Aarti Sathe accepted the challenge. The High Court held that the show cause notice itself had been issued without jurisdiction and that the proceedings were therefore void from the outset. The tax department had relied on Section 87 of the CGST Act to contend that liabilities relating to the period before the merger could still be pursued. The High Court, however, held that the provision did not authorise the department to issue a show-cause notice to a company that had ceased to exist after amalgamation The Union of India was represented by Additional Solicitor General Dwarakanath. items.title: Satya Niketan building collapse: PIL in Delhi HC seeks ₹1 cr compensation; audit of PGs, hostels
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Monday agreed to hear a public interest litigation (PIL) petition concerning the collapse of a multi-storey Paying Guest (PG) building in South West Delhi's Satya Niketan. The PIL filed by one Aniket Kumar Gupta has sought ₹1 crore compensation for the kin of the victims of the collapse besides a structural audit of all PG accommodations/ hostels. The plea was mentioned for urgent hearing before a Bench of Chief Justice DK Upadhyay and Justice Tejas Karia . According to reports, at least six people have died in the building collapse near Delhi University‘s South Campus. An FIR has been registered against the person who ran the PG accommodation. Gupta in the PIL said that preliminary reports indicate that repair, renovation or construction-related work was allegedly being undertaken in the building immediately before the collapse. "Questions have arisen regarding the legality of such work, the structural integrity of the premises, compliance with sanctioned building plans, use of the premises as a PG/hostel, existence of structural stability certifications, fire safety compliance and the adequacy of inspections conducted by the concerned statutory authorities," the plea said. Besides compensation to the kin, the petitioner has sought an independent and comprehensive investigation into the causes leading to the collapse, including the role of owners, builders, contractors, architects, structural engineers, persons involved in renovation work and public authorities responsible for inspection and enforcement of building regulations. items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Monday directed a trial court to reconsider Malayalam actress Ansiba Hassan's plea for the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) against actress Lakshmi Priya and two representatives of an online media outlet, Can Channel Media [ Ansiba Hassan v State of Kerala & ors ]. items.title: Courts must resist rehearing arbitral awards on merits to build global arbitration hub: Darius Khambata
items.summary: If India has to develop as a preferred arbitration seat, courts in the country must resist the temptation to re-hear arbitration disputes on merits, Senior Advocate Darius Khambata said on September 5 . The senior lawyer was speaking at the Gujarat High Court Arbitration Centre (GHAC) Arbitration Week in GIFT City on ‘Rules of Private International Law in International Commercial Arbitration. He explained that non-interference from courts means resisting the temptation to decide the matter. “In arbitration, the justice of the case requires that a court respect the decision of the parties that an arbitral tribunal decides, and not a judge. That's the justice of the case,” he added. Khambata urged courts to explicitly frame challenge grounds immediately instead of re-hearing the entire disputes on merits. “If you have a good judicial ecosystem and a good legislative ecosystem that really makes for a very successful seat,” he said. He also highlighted Singapore’s practice of institutional humility. “With all its success, every single month and year the Singaporeans are thinking of how we can improve? Where have we gone wrong? items.title: Unemployed woman's land cannot be assumed to be joint family asset: Karnataka High Court
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently observed that the mere fact that a woman was unemployed and had no independent source of income is not sufficient to hold that property purchased in her name was acquired from joint-family funds [ Rajesh Exports v B Devaraj ]. The Bench of Justices Jayant Banerji and Tara Vitasta Ganju made the observation while setting aside a 2009 trial court decree passed in favour of two sons and the wife of one S Balasubramanya over certain property in Bengaluru. Balasubramanya had inherited the said property from his mother, Lalithamma. In 2004, he sold the property to a company, Rajesh Exports. Balasubramanya went missing shortly thereafter. His two sons and wife (plaintiffs), however, challenged the sale of the property to Rajesh Exports. They argued that the land was a joint family asset in which they held rights, and which could not have been unilaterally sold by Balasubramanya. They filed a suit before a civil court asserting a share in the said property. The legal question central to the case, therefore, was whether the disputed property was an asset belonging to the Hindu joint family or not. A trial court in 2009 held that the property was a joint family asset, and ruled that Balasubramanya's sons and wife were entitled to a 1/4th share. The trial court reasoned that Lalithamma, in whose name the property was registered before Balasubramanya inherited it, was an unemployed housewife with no independent source of income. As such, the trial court proceeded on the assumption that the property registered in her name was purchased using the joint family's pool of funds (the joint Hindu family's nucleus of funds), making it a joint family asset. Rajesh Exports challenged this ruling before the High Court, which on August 29 ruled that the trial court's approach was flawed. "Merely to assume, that because Smt. items.summary: Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra was sworn in as the Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court by Punjab Governor Gulab Chand Kataria on Monday morning. items.title: ‘I was shocked’: Justice RV Raveendran disagrees with Justice Nariman on full appeal against arbitral awards
items.summary: Former Supreme Court judge Justice RV Raveendran on Sunday disagreed with Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman’s recent suggestion for a full-fledged first appeal against domestic arbitral awards on facts and law, saying such a remedy would defeat the very purpose of arbitration. Justice Raveendran said he was “shocked” by the suggestion, though he acknowledged that it reflected the frustration caused by the present state of challenges to arbitral awards. “ Imagine, out of desperation, Justice Nariman said, let us have a first one appeal, full appeal and be done with it. I was shocked. But see, that is the amount of desperation .” He added, “ If you have a first appeal, then why have an arbitration? The entire purpose of arbitration is to have finality .” Justice RV Raveendran Justice Raveendran said that if courts were given wider appellate powers, including the ability to extensively reconsider or modify awards, the distinction between arbitration and ordinary litigation would begin to disappear. He was speaking at a panel discussion titled “A Judge’s wish list of what the law ought to be” on the concluding day of GHAC Arbitration Week 2026 in Gandhinagar. The three-day conference, held from September 4 to 6 at GIFT City Club, was organised by the Gujarat High Court in collaboration with the Gujarat High Court Arbitration Centre. items.title: Supreme Court’s recent arbitration rulings have created grave uncertainty: Retired Justice Rohinton Nariman
items.summary: Former Supreme Court Justice Rohinton F Nariman recently said that some of the Supreme Court’s recent arbitration judgments were incorrect and had created “grave uncertainty” by reopening settled questions. Justice Nariman was delivering the keynote address at the Gujarat High Court Arbitration Centre’s Arbitration Week 2026. He examined 5 recent Constitution Bench decisions concerning the appointment of arbitrators and challenges to arbitral awards. “ Here we have five recent judgments of the Supreme Court. How has the Act fared? According to me, not particularly well, because, firstly, the judgments don’t conduce to certainty . Secondly, constantly reopening closed questions again leads to grave uncertainty. Some of the judgments, unfortunately, are on the face of them not correct, in my humble submission," he said. Justice Nariman first referred to the five-judge ruling in Cox and Kings . The judgment held that the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 had to be read with the Contract Act while deciding whether a non-signatory intended to be bound by an arbitration agreement. He contrasted this with the subsequent 7-judge ruling on unstamped arbitration agreements. That judgment described the Arbitration Act as a self-contained code and special enactment. Justice Nariman said that this reasoning contradicted Cox and Kings , where the Contract Act had been treated as fundamental to determining the existence of an arbitration agreement. He also criticised the speed with which the earlier 5-judge ruling in NN Global was reopened by a seven-judge bench. He said, “ Unfortunately, what was made certain by 5 judges was made uncertain. items.title: BAPS and its celibate monks: The organisation at the centre of the Eiffel Tower row
items.summary: A Hindu religious organisation has come under fire in Paris, France after female employees at the Eiffel Tower were allegedly asked to move away or make themselves “invisible” during a private visit by its delegation. This prompted staff to strike and force the iconic landmark to close on September 7. The delegation, comprising around 100 people, was from the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha, or BAPS, a Hindu religious organisation with roots in Gujarat and a large global following. French authorities are investigating the incident after employees said they were instructed to make themselves “invisible” while the delegation passed through the landmark. BAPS is a denomination within the Swaminarayan tradition of Hinduism. A Hindu group with several branches in the UK and US it gets millions in donations and grants every year. Recently, the massive BAPS Swaminarayan temple in Paris was inaugurated. Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the inauguration through a video message and described the temple as a milestone in India-France cultural relations. He said the teachings and “Indian cultural” message emerging from the temple would benefit people across Europe. The organisation has apologised for the controversy but said that, to its knowledge, no one was prevented from accessing the Eiffel Tower. It said the visit was organised with the tower’s management because of the size of the delegation and was scheduled at the beginning of normal opening hours to minimise disruption to other visitors. So, what exactly is BAPS, why do their monks have strict celibacy vows that prevent interaction with women, and what kind of relationship do they share with the Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi? What is BAPS? The wider Swaminarayan tradition emerged in Gujarat in the late 18th and early 19th centuries around Sahajanand Swami, known as Bhagwan Swaminarayan. BAPS traces its formal establishment to 1907, when Shastriji Maharaj, one of Swaminarayan’s spiritual successors, established a temple in Bochasan, Gujarat. The organisation takes its name from the town and its central theological idea, the Akshar-Purushottam philosophy. BAPS describes itself as a “socio-spiritual Hindu faith” rooted in the Vedas. According to BAPS, it currently has more than 5,000 centres globally and more than a million followers. Its most visible presence is perhaps its temples. items.title: Opinion: Mohan Bhagwat’s speech on oneness barely hides his Hindutva sophistry
items.summary: Several press reports and prominent commentators on Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) sarsanghchalak Mohan Bhagwat’s speech at New York’s Madison Square Garden tell us that his words on ‘oneness in diversity’ mark a welcome departure from hardline Hindu supremacism. Others believe that Bhagwat has given the RSS a liberal spin in the US, in words he would not use in India. Both these assessments are off the mark. Bhagwat has given near-identical speeches several times in India, including earlier this year. Indeed he told his US audience as much, recalling his 2018 speech given at Nagpur. He uses the same formulations in both the US and India, but in the latter, he is more expansive. Place one next to the other, and the Hindu supremacist sophistry becomes unmistakeable. ‘Oneness’ vs ‘unity’ The concept of ‘universal oneness’ can mean that all beings, all things, and all spiritual traditions are equally valid expressions of the same perennial philosophy, the same inner oneness. It would follow that the Hindu traditions too would be one among such diverse expressions. But that’s not what Bhagwat said. A t the NYC event, he said the Hindu tradition is synonymous with the philosophy of oneness. Hindus, he said, safeguarded this philosophy from “foreign invaders”, and generously shared it with the rest of the world. In his 2018 iteration of this point, he explained that the RSS “insists on the name ‘Hindu’” to stand for all the traditions born in Bharat (“ Bharat mein janmein sabhi panth-sampradayon ka naam hindutva hai” ). The RSS, he said, considered “Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Sanatanis, and Arya Samajis” to be Hindu, but these communities were free to call themselves ‘Bharatiya’ if they so preferred. Speaking at a ‘100 Years of the Sangh Journey’ event in February this year, he said that ‘everyone living in India is Hindu,’ and all would have to accept Hindutva as their national/civilisational identity sooner or later. He assured Muslims and Christians, as well as Sikhs, Jains, Buddhists, and Parsis, that they could practice their religion while “accepting Hindutva”, and in fact “Hindutva is a guarantee of your safety.” If they do not accept Hindutva, is Bhagwat implying that there is no guarantee of their safety? items.summary: Women in Kerala's colleges are grappling with a new form of digital harassment, as generative AI is increasingly used to create and circulate non-consensual morphed images of students and faculty. These cases of digital morphing reported from across the state have led to arrests but are being invoked by orthodox voices to argue for greater restrictions on women’s public participation. The most recent incident relates to the arrest of Ajmal T Muhammad, a fourth-year engineering student at Mangalam College of Engineering, Ettumanoor, Kottayam. He was arrested following complaints that he photographed female classmates during campus events and used AI software to alter the images into explicit content. Recently, Kochi police arrested Srihari S, a second-year student at Bharata Mata College, Thrikkakara, and later detained a co-accused, Saneesh, from Alappuzha in a similar complaint. Investigators said Srihari used his position on the college's student media team to collect photographs of female classmates and faculty members, which were then altered using AI tools and circulated in private Telegram groups. In July, at Trivandrum Medical College, an MBBS student Abel Augustine was arrested after fellow students discovered altered images being circulated on Reddit and Telegram. According to reports, similar allegations have come up from around 12 other colleges in the state after Onam celebrations. The presence of Muslim women at public functions, including Milad and Onam celebrations, has recently sparked a debate in Kerala. What began with a circular issued by the Samastha Kerala Jem-iyyathul Ulama, directing mosques to prevent women from sharing public spaces with unrelated men, has now opened up a wider debate on gender and women’s participation in public life in the state. Ansari Zuhri, a social media influencer known for content related to Kerala’s Muslim community, was among the first to draw a connection between women’s dance performances and the crime. items.title: CMRL case: ED writes to Keralam DGP, seeks FIR against Pinarayi Vijayan
items.summary: The Enforcement Directorate has written to police chief of Keralam seeking to register a case against Leader of Opposition and former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, his son-in-law and MLA Mohammed Riyas and his daughter T Veena in connection with the Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL) payoff case. State Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala said the director general of police has confirmed receiving a letter from ED on Tuesday, September 8. “Let us examine the letter. Necessary legal steps will be taken after that,” Chennithaal said. As per the document shared by TV channels, the charges against Pinarayi Vijayan were based on the admission of P Suresh Kumar, former Chief Financial Officer of CMRL. As per ED’s note, Vijayan received Rs 3.28 crore bribe from CMRL through his daughter Veena. According to ED, Veena’s husband and MLA Mohammed Riyas received bribes and transferred the funds to Dubai through Veena and his associates. The ED has accused Veena of assisting Vijayan and Mohammed Riyas in collecting and routing of bribe funds. The ED has sought to register a first information report (FIR) under the Prevention of Corruption Act and other relevant laws. Names of 13 individuals and entities are part of the ED’s letter. These include CMRL managing director Sasidharan Kartha, former CFO Suresh Kumar, Veena’s now defunct IT firm Exalogic Solutions and some individuals whom ED listed as those who assisted Riyas in transferring funds. In May, investigating officers under ED conducted searches at the residence of Pinarayi Vijayan in Thiruvananthapuram and his ancestral home in Kannur. This led to intense protest by workers of Communist Party of India (Marxist), which ended up in an attack on ED officers in Thiruvananthapuram. Around 18 CPIM workers were arrested for attacking ED officers. The alleged CMRL-Exalogic payoff case began with an inspection of the Income Tax department at CMRL which found that it paid around Rs 1.72 crore to Exalogic between 2017-2020. Later ED began an investigation into the allegation that the money was a pay off to Pinarayi Vijayan. In addition to a monthly payment of Rs 3 lakh to Exalogic, CMRL has paid Veena a remuneration of Rs 5 lakh per month for IT consultancy services. As per ED’s report, there was no evidence that Exalogic or Veena actually provided IT services to CMRL during this period.

items.title: Mass tourism is hurting Kannur’s Madayippara, an eco heritage status can change it
items.summary: On a holiday, the road around Madayippara can become a parking lot. Hundreds of vehicles line the roadside as visitors make their way towards the biodiversity-rich laterite plateau in Kannur, drawn by its seasonal flowers, open landscape, and photographs of the place that have increasingly found their way into tourism promotions and social media feeds. But for those fighting to protect Madayippara, the crowds are a warning. The concern is not merely about litter, traffic or the inconvenience caused by visitors. It is about what happens to a fragile ecosystem when a landscape never meant to accommodate mass tourism begins attracting it in growing numbers, even as commercial projects emerge around it. Madayippara is a flat laterite hillock spread across around 365 hectares near Payangadi, about 22 km north of Kannur town. Once known mainly for its religious, cultural and ecological significance, it has increasingly become a tourist attraction, drawing visitors from Kerala and elsewhere, including tourists from outside India. That anxiety brought residents, environmentalists and others together for a rally on August 22, demanding to drop the proposed Eco Park project in the area and for a greater protection of Madayippara. “The panchayat secretary has temporarily issued a stop memo for the eco-park as a result of our protests,” environmentalist VC Balakrishnan told The News Minute. The stop memo has not, however, ended the larger concerns surrounding the plateau. According to Balakrishnan, even with police preventing vehicles from entering Madayippara following a High Court order, the number of people arriving remains high. “On holidays, there are often between 500 and 900 vehicles parked along the roadside there. Earlier, vehicles used to be allowed to enter Madayippara, but now the police are maintaining vigilance based on a High Court order, and vehicles are not being allowed to enter Madayippara,” he said. “However, huge crowds still come. Thousands of people, especially on holidays, visit the place.” ‘Madayippara is not a tourist centre’ That is at the heart of the activists’ argument: Madayippara, they say, is being treated as a tourist destination when it is actually a living ecosystem. “Our argument is that Madayippara is not a tourist centre.
